content.title: Main Takeaways UNC Advances to Sweet 16 with 7466 Win Over Maryland
content.text: CHAPEL HILL — North Carolina is headed back to the Sweet 16 after a 74–66 win over Maryland in the second round of the NCAA Tournament Sunday afternoon at Carmichael Arena. In a physical game that stayed close throughout, the Tar Heels used a strong fourth quarter, efficient offense, and senior leadership to pull away late and advance to the second weekend of the NCAA Tournament for the second straight season.North Carolina led for over 31 minutes but had to respond when Maryland briefly took the lead in the fourth quarter. The Tar Heels answered with a late run to close out the game strong at Carmichael Arena.Here are the main takeaways from UNC's win over Maryland.Fourth Quarter Execution Sealed the WinWith the game tied entering the fourth quarter, North Carolina took control in the final 10 minutes. The Tar Heels outscored Maryland 24–16 in the fourth quarter and shot over 60 percent from the field in the final period.Maryland briefly took the lead early in the fourth quarter, but UNC answered with a run that included a fast-break three from Nyla Brooks, a layup from Lanie Grant, and several key late free throws. Nyla Harris's fast-break layup helped seal the game.Lanie Grant said the team remained calm when Maryland made a run in the fourth quarter."We knew it would be a dog fight throughout the entire time," Grant said. "So even though we were up by double digits, we knew we couldn't let up. They gave us a good run, and we kind of just did a good job of absorbing that and not panicking, not trying to do too much, not getting away from the game plan."UNC's ability to stay composed, get defensive stops, and execute offensively late in the game was the difference in a matchup that was tied after three quarters.Paint Scoring and Efficiency Made the DifferenceNorth Carolina did not rely heavily on the three-point shot in this game; instead, it attacked the paint and scored efficiently. The Tar Heels attempted just 11 three-pointers but finished the game shooting 49 percent from the field and scored 44 points in the paint.Maryland struggled shooting throughout the game, finishing just 32 percent from the field and 3-for-23 from three-point range. While Maryland kept the game close by crashing the offensive glass and scoring 21 second-chance points, UNC's efficiency and ability to finish at the rim proved to be the difference.The Tar Heels adjusted offensively and attacked one-on-one matchups, which allowed players like Lanie Grant and Elina Aarnisalo to get to the rim and score inside.Aarnisalo said Maryland's defensive style created opportunities for UNC to attack the paint."Their defensive style gave us an opportunity to attack the paint and go one-on-one against them," Aarnisalo said. "There were times Lanie and I had the ball and saw the paint empty, and it's go time at that point."Head coach Courtney Banghart said the game plan was to spread the floor and attack matchups one-on-one."If no one is guarding you, find someone to guard you and go by them," Banghart said. "We wanted to stay spaced and spread them out."Balanced Scoring Continues to Be UNC's StrengthNorth Carolina had four players score in double figures in the win, continuing a trend that has led to success for the Tar Heels this season.Elina Aarnisalo led UNC with 21 points, followed by Lanie Grant with 20 points, Nyla Harris with 14 points, and Indya Nivar with 11 points. North Carolina is now 10–1 this season when four players score in double figures, showing how important balanced scoring has been to the team's success.Rather than relying on one player, multiple Tar Heels stepped up, especially in the fourth quarter when UNC needed key baskets and free throws to secure the win.Grant also pointed to the team's ability to rely on each other in big moments."The biggest thing was getting stops and securing rebounds," Grant said. "We just kept leaning on each other."A Sweet 16 Team Built Through DevelopmentAfter the game, head coach Courtney Banghart emphasized that this Sweet 16 team was built through recruiting and player development rather than through the transfer portal. Banghart said only two players on the roster, Nyla Harris and Elina Aarnisalo, were transfers, and that North Carolina is the seventh youngest Power Four team in the country.Banghart also explained how much the team improved throughout the season through development and film work. She said the staff films everything and even joked that she almost had the practice gym redone because there were no cameras in it, so they could record practices and show players what they were doing right and wrong."We were not good in June," Banghart said. "It takes a special group to make up as much ground as they've made. I'm really proud of our recruiting and really proud of our development to put us in this position."That development throughout the season has helped a young North Carolina team grow into a Sweet 16 team despite losing major production from last season.Senior Leadership Delivered in CarmichaelSeniors Indya Nivar and Nyla Harris were key in helping North Carolina close out the game and advance to the Sweet 16, showing the leadership they've displayed all season when Maryland briefly took the lead in the fourth quarter.Nivar fouled out late in the fourth quarter in what was her final game at Carmichael Arena. After the game, Banghart said it was fitting because Nivar "didn't leave anything on the floor" and had given everything to the program."It's really fitting she fouled out of her last game at Carmichael because she didn't leave anything on the floor," Banghart said. "She left it all out there."With a young roster, leadership from Nivar and Harris has been crucial to North Carolina's Sweet 16 run.Quick Stats:Final Score: North Carolina 74, Maryland 66FG %: UNC 49%, Maryland 32%Points in the Paint: UNC 44, Maryland 34Second Chance Points: Maryland 21, UNC 10Lead Changes: 6Times Tied: 5Four Tar Heels scored in double figures: Aarnisalo (21 points), Grant (20), Harris (14), and Nivar (11).UNC Record: 28–7With the win, the Tar Heels are headed to Fort Worth for the Sweet 16, where they will face the winner of No. 1 UConn and No. 9 Syracuse on Friday. Tipoff time and television details will be announced after the completion of the second-round games.
